facets.core_claim: Dragon and fairy could not dwell together; Lạc Long Quân led fifty sons to the sea while Âu Cơ led fifty to the mountains, dividing and peopling the land.

facets.facet_name: Mountain Fairy, Mother of the Hundred Sons
facets.core_claim: From Âu Cơ's hundred eggs came the hundred ancestors of the Viet; she is "Mẹ Âu Cơ", mother of the nation, who led half her children to the highlands.

facets.facet_name: Heavenly Princess Who Chose to Return to Earth
facets.core_claim: Exiled from heaven for a broken cup, Liễu Hạnh came down by choice again and again, living among humans; she is the goddess who refuses to stay away.

facets.facet_name: Holy Mother of the Four Palaces
facets.core_claim: As Mẫu Liễu Hạnh she presides over the Four Palaces; in lên đồng mediumship she and her court descend into the mediums.

facets.facet_name: The Fourfold Cosmos of the Mother Goddesses
facets.core_claim: The Mothers of the Four Palaces divide the cosmos into sky, mountain-forest, water and earth, governing all through their spirit court.

facets.facet_name: Mother of the Mountains and Forests
facets.core_claim: The green-robed Mother of the Upper Forests governs mountains, trees and creatures and blesses the people of the highlands.

facets.facet_name: Mother of the Water Palace
facets.core_claim: Daughter of the Dragon King, Mẫu Thoải rules the waters of the Four Palaces and keeps boats and farmers' fields watered.

facets.facet_name: Silent Child Who Became a Giant Savior
facets.core_claim: At the nation's need the mute child grew in a moment into a giant warrior, defeated the invaders and ascended to heaven; he is one of the Four Immortals.

facets.facet_name: Deified General Who Commands the Spirit Armies
facets.core_claim: Saint Trần, victor over the Mongols, now leads the spirit hosts against demons and sickness; his temples at Kiếp Bạc and Bảo Lộc are centers of exorcism.

facets.facet_name: Kitchen Gods Who Report to Heaven
facets.core_claim: From the hearth the Táo watch the household all year and at Tết ride their carp up to the Jade Emperor to report.

facets.facet_name: Mountain Spirit Who Holds Back the Floods
facets.core_claim: Each rainy season Sơn Tinh lifts the hills against the waters of his rival, keeping the people safe.

facets.facet_name: Jilted Water Spirit of the Annual Floods
facets.core_claim: Thủy Tinh's unending jealousy brings the yearly floods of the Red River, as he tries again to seize what he lost.

facets.facet_name: Holy Mother of Nha Trang
facets.core_claim: Thiên Y A Na gave the people of the coast rice farming and weaving and protects them from her tower-temple at Nha Trang.

facets.facet_name: Guardian God of the Village Communal House
facets.core_claim: The Thành Hoàng, invested by imperial patent, watches over the village from the đình and receives its offerings and festivals.

facets.facet_name: Bathala Maykapal, Creator of All
facets.core_claim: Bathala made the world and humanity and rules from above; the anito are his intermediaries among people.
facets.scholarly_note: Spanish chroniclers reported Bathala as the highest deity; the details of his family (Apolaki, Mayari, Tala as children) come from 20th-century compilations.

facets.facet_name: Androgynous Deity of Fertile Fields
facets.core_claim: Farmers offer to Lakapati when they sow, praying that fields will yield and that the community will be fed.

facets.facet_name: One-Eyed Moon Who Shares the Sky
facets.core_claim: After her battle with Apolaki, Mayari rules the night with her one remaining eye while he rules the day.
facets.scholarly_note: The sibling-war narrative comes from 20th-century compilations; Mayari as a moon deity is reported from Tagalog and Kapampangan areas.

facets.facet_name: Sun God and Patron of Warriors
facets.core_claim: Apolaki rides across the day as the sun and gives courage to warriors; he and Mayari divide the sky between day and night.

facets.facet_name: Goddess of the Stars and Morning Star
facets.core_claim: Tala lights the stars and guides those who travel and work before sunrise.

facets.facet_name: Keeper of Kasamaan and Its Four Agents
facets.core_claim: Sitan rules Kasamaan and sends his four agents among humans to bring sickness, discord and death.
facets.scholarly_note: The name may reflect Spanish "Satanás"; the four-agent scheme comes from 20th-century compilations.

facets.facet_name: Visayan Sovereign of the Sky
facets.core_claim: Kaptan rules the sky; from his contest with the sea-lord the islands of the world were formed, and from a bamboo stalk the first man and woman emerged.

facets.facet_name: Sea Serpent That Swallows the Moon
facets.core_claim: Bakunawa's hunger causes eclipses; only the clamor of the people forces it to release the moon.

facets.facet_name: The One Unthinkable God (Acintya)
facets.core_claim: All gods are rays of Sang Hyang Widhi; as Acintya he cannot be conceived, and the empty seat at the top of the padmasana is his.

facets.facet_name: King of the Gods in Jonggringsaloka
facets.core_claim: Batara Guru sits enthroned over the Javanese heavens, ordering the world, sending gods on missions and judging their disputes.

facets.facet_name: The God Hidden in a Clown's Body
facets.core_claim: Semar's lowly, laughable form hides the eldest divinity; he serves the heroes, guards Java, and even Batara Guru must bow to his rebuke.

facets.facet_name: Rice Goddess Whose Body Became the Crop
facets.core_claim: From the grave of Dewi Sri grew rice and the food plants; she lives in every rice field and granary and must be honored at planting and harvest.

facets.facet_name: Queen of the Southern Sea and Consort of Kings
facets.core_claim: The Queen of the South Sea grants sovereignty to the Mataram kings through spiritual marriage and claims the drowned who wear her green.

facets.facet_name: Widow-Witch Queen of the Graveyard
facets.core_claim: Rangda commands the leyak and black magic, yet as a manifestation of Durga her terrible power also guards the village.

facets.facet_name: Lion Spirit Who Protects the Village
facets.core_claim: The Barong defends the village against Rangda and illness; his sacred mask is kept in the temple and brought out to purify the land.

facets.facet_name: World Serpent Beneath the Earth
facets.core_claim: From the lowest underworld Antaboga upholds the world; the cosmic turtle and the rice goddess come from him.

facets.facet_name: Devouring Giant of Time
facets.core_claim: Kala devours the unprotected; only the ruwatan performance, which tells his story and pacifies him, releases those he may claim.

facets.facet_name: Supreme God of the Upperworld (the Hornbill)
facets.core_claim: Mahatala rules the Upperworld; with Jata of the Underworld he forms the totality of the godhead, and from their encounter came the tree of life and the first humans.

facets.facet_name: Watersnake Queen of the Underworld
facets.core_claim: Jata rules the waters and the world below; with Mahatala she makes up the whole divine reality.

facets.facet_name: The Great Beginning, Creator of the Three Worlds
facets.core_claim: All beings come from Mulajadi na Bolon, who brought forth the gods of the three worlds; the Parmalim pray to him as the one God.

facets.facet_name: Holy Guardian Spirit of a Place
facets.core_claim: Each keramat watches over its locality; those who honor his shrine are protected and their requests heard.

facets.facet_name: King of the Nats, Who Descends at Thingyan
facets.core_claim: Thagyamin heads the nats as a guardian of the Buddha's religion and descends at the New Year to judge the deeds of humankind.

facets.facet_name: Royal Pantheon of Spirits Born of Violent Death
facets.core_claim: Born of tragic deaths, the nats hold great power over luck, health and the land; honored and fed, they protect, neglected, they punish.

facets.facet_name: Guardian Nat of Every Household
facets.core_claim: The burned blacksmith became the house-nat: a green coconut hung on the house pillar honors Mahagiri, who protects the family.

facets.facet_name: Mother Nat of Mount Popa
facets.core_claim: Popa Medaw reigns over Mount Popa, the home of the nats, honored by pilgrims and mediums.

facets.facet_name: Earth Goddess Who Wrung Out Her Hair
facets.core_claim: Called by the earth-touching gesture, Mae Thorani bore witness to the Buddha's merit and drowned Mara's host in the waters stored in her hair.

facets.facet_name: Spirits of Land, House and Village
facets.core_claim: The phi of each place must be honored at the spirit house; when respected they guard the household, when slighted they bring illness and misfortune.

facets.facet_name: Rice Mother Who Holds the Grain's Soul
facets.core_claim: Mae Phosop is the life in the rice; she must be treated gently and honored, or she will leave the fields and famine will follow.

facets.facet_name: Naga King of the Mekong
facets.core_claim: Phaya Nak holds the river and rain in his power and guards the Buddha's relics and the peoples of the Mekong.

facets.facet_name: Ancestral Guardians of the Land
facets.core_claim: The Neak Ta own and protect each piece of Khmer land; the community honors them so that rain falls and harm stays away.

facets.facet_name: Mother of the Cham Kingdom
facets.core_claim: Po Nagar brought the land and its riches into being and protects the kingdom from her temple on the hill at Nha Trang.

facets.facet_name: Atua of the Ocean and Its Creatures
facets.core_claim: All fish and sea creatures are the children of Tangaroa; his waves contend with Tāne's land, and his tapu governs fishing.

facets.facet_name: Atua of War and of Humankind
facets.core_claim: Tū alone withstood the storm and subdued his brothers' offspring, so that humans, his descendants, may hunt, fish, cultivate and make war.

facets.facet_name: Lord of Darkness and Disease
facets.core_claim: Whiro is the source of all evil, sickness and death; from Rarohenga he battles Tāne's light and devours the dead.

facets.facet_name: Storm Who Avenged the Parted Parents
facets.core_claim: Loyal to his father the Sky, Tāwhirimātea makes war with storm and hurricane on all his brothers who agreed to the separation.

facets.facet_name: Atua of Uncultivated Foods
facets.core_claim: Bracken root and wild food are the children of Haumia; they sustain the people in lean times.

facets.facet_name: Unborn Son Whose Stirring Shakes the Earth
facets.core_claim: Rūaumoko lives within Papatūānuku; when he moves, the land shakes and fire rises from below.

facets.facet_name: Ancestress Who Keeps Fire in Her Nails
facets.core_claim: Fire comes from Mahuika's nails; tricked by Māui, she let fire loose and hid it in the kaikōmako, māhoe and tōtara trees for humanity.

facets.facet_name: God of the Deep Ocean and Companion of Kāne
facets.core_claim: Kanaloa rules the deep sea and guides voyagers; with Kāne he walks the islands, opening fresh springs and drinking ʻawa.

facets.facet_name: Kanaloa as Leader of Rebellious Spirits (Kepelino)
facets.core_claim: In Kepelino's telling Kanaloa led the spirits in rebellion against Kāne, Kū and Lono and was cast down to the underworld.
facets.scholarly_note: This account is widely judged to reflect Christian influence on the Catholic-educated author; earlier Hawaiian practice honors Kanaloa positively.

facets.facet_name: Mother Goddess of Birth and Renewal
facets.core_claim: Haumea brings forth children and plants, taught true childbirth, and is reborn young again and again to mate with her descendants.

facets.facet_name: Lord of the Underworld Lua-o-Milu
facets.core_claim: In Lua-o-Milu the unguided dead come under the rule of Milu, below the land of the living.

facets.facet_name: Sky Father and Ancestor of the Chiefs
facets.core_claim: With Papa, Wākea begot the islands; through Hāloa, the taro and the first man, all Hawaiians descend from him.

facets.facet_name: Earth Mother Who Gave Birth to Islands
facets.core_claim: Papa birthed the Hawaiian islands from her body; the land itself is her child and the people her descendants.

facets.facet_name: Shape-Shifting Pig God of Rain and Lover of Pele
facets.core_claim: Kamapuaʻa's rains and wild energy oppose and unite with Pele's fire; their struggle divides the islands into wet and dry.

facets.facet_name: Snow Goddess Who Contends with Pele
facets.core_claim: From Mauna Kea Poliʻahu answers Pele's fire with snow and cold, keeping balance on the island of Hawaiʻi.

facets.facet_name: Goddess of Hula and Healing Who Revived the Dead
facets.core_claim: Hiʻiaka's chants heal and restore life; the hula is hers, and she cleared the islands of monsters on her great journey.

facets.facet_name: Shark God Who Guides Voyagers
facets.core_claim: Kamohoaliʻi leads lost canoes home and guards those who honor him; he is the greatest of shark ʻaumakua.

facets.facet_name: Ruler of Pulotu, Realm of the Dead
facets.core_claim: In Pulotu Hikuleʻo receives the spirits of the chiefs and rules the world beneath, as Tangaloa rules above and Maui on earth.

facets.facet_name: Eel-Bodied Lord of the Underworld
facets.core_claim: Saveasiʻuleo receives the spirits of the dead in Pulotu beneath the western sea.

facets.facet_name: War Goddess Who Distributed Sovereignty
facets.core_claim: Victorious Nafanua conferred the great titles of Samoa and prophesied a new kingdom from heaven.
facets.scholarly_note: Samoan Christians later read her prophecy as foretelling the arrival of the missionaries (1830).

facets.facet_name: Sky God Who Fathered the Sacred Kings
facets.core_claim: From the heavens Tangaloa descended to father the line of the Tuʻi Tonga and sent down the islands as wood-chips from his workbench.

facets.facet_name: Self-Created God Who Broke His Shell
facets.core_claim: Alone in the void Taʻaroa created himself, burst his shell and fashioned the cosmos from the shell and from his own body.

facets.facet_name: War God and Patron of the ʻArioi
facets.core_claim: ʻOro gives victory and receives sacrifice; through his son-like devotees, the ʻArioi, he also presides over festivity and the renewal of fertility.

facets.facet_name: Creator God of the Birdman Cult
facets.core_claim: Makemake made the first humans and brings the birds each spring; the Birdman contest at ʻOrongo is held in his honor.

facets.facet_name: Primordial Darkness and Lord of the Sea
facets.core_claim: Before all things was Tanaoa, darkness and the deep; light (Atea) and sound (Ono) emerged by overcoming him.

facets.facet_name: Light Who Became the Sky Father
facets.core_claim: Atea rose as light, drove Tanaoa's darkness away, and as Sky Father begot the gods and the Marquesan people.

facets.facet_name: The Very Beginning at the Root of the Cosmos
facets.core_claim: At the base of the cosmic coconut dwells Vari; from pieces of her own flesh she made the first gods and the world above her.

facets.facet_name: Sky God of Knowledge Who Came to Earth
facets.core_claim: Lugeilan, keeper of heavenly knowledge, descends from heaven to the world of humans; his son by a mortal woman is Olifat.
facets.scholarly_note: Names and genealogies differ across the Caroline Islands; Chuukese Luk is often treated as a cognate of Lugeilan.

facets.facet_name: Trickster Who Climbed to Heaven on Smoke
facets.core_claim: Olifat breaks every rule between heaven and earth: mischievous, cruel and generous, he gave the world fire and its dangers.

facets.facet_name: Primordial Brother Whose Body Became the World
facets.core_claim: Puntan gave his body to become the cosmos: sky, earth, sun, moon and rainbow are Puntan.

facets.facet_name: Sister Who Shaped the World and Birthed Humanity
facets.core_claim: Fuʻuna crafted the cosmos from Puntan and became the stone from which the Chamorro people emerged.

facets.facet_name: Serpent Creator in the Mountain Cave
facets.core_claim: From his cave Degei created humanity and sustains the world; his stirring causes earthquakes and thunder.

facets.facet_name: Judge of the Passing Souls
facets.core_claim: Every soul leaving Fiji passes Degei, who questions it and sends it to Murimuria or to punishment.

facets.facet_name: Shark God and Guardian of Fishermen
facets.core_claim: Dakuwaqa patrols the reefs; those under his protection, above all the people of Kadavu, are never harmed by sharks.

facets.facet_name: Spider Whose Buried Figures Brought Death
facets.core_claim: Copying Qat but burying his carvings, Marawa caused them to decay, and decay and death entered the world.

facets.facet_name: The Wise Culture-Hero Brother
facets.core_claim: To Kabinana fashions what is good and right in the world, and his wisdom sets the pattern for the Tolai.

facets.facet_name: The Foolish Brother Who Botched Creation
facets.core_claim: To Purgo's clumsy imitations produced the shark and the evils of the world, which his brother could not undo.

facets.facet_name: Sky Being of Initiation and Law
facets.core_claim: Daramulan established the initiation ceremonies and oversees the keeping of the law from the sky.

facets.core_claim: Waa and Bunjil divide the Kulin world into two halves; Waa's cunning brought fire to everyone.

facets.facet_name: Ancestor Who Shaped the River and Went to the Sky
facets.core_claim: Ngurunderi's journey made the Murray, its lakes and the Coorong and laid down the law; he showed the way the spirits of the dead go to the sky.
facets.scholarly_note: Drawn only from published, publicly available (non-restricted) material; restricted and secret-sacred knowledge is deliberately excluded. Authority over these narratives rests with the custodians of the relevant Country, and versions differ between language groups.

facets.facet_name: Mouthless Beings of Rain and Law
facets.core_claim: The Wandjina bring the wet season and the renewal of life and enforce the law; their painted images are their living presence.

facets.facet_name: Great Python Who Brings the Monsoon
facets.core_claim: Yurlunggur rises from his waterhole into the sky as the monsoon cloud and lightning, swallowing and restoring, making the seasons turn.

facets.facet_name: Sisters Whose Journey Named the Land
facets.core_claim: Walking and naming, the Sisters brought the country and its creatures into ordered being; their swallowing by the python is the turning of the year.
facets.scholarly_note: Drawn only from published, publicly available (non-restricted) material; restricted and secret-sacred knowledge is deliberately excluded. Authority over these narratives rests with the custodians of the relevant Country, and versions differ between language groups.

facets.facet_name: Creator Serpent of the Deep Pools
facets.core_claim: Ngalyod made the country and still lives in its waters, giving rain and life and punishing those who disturb sacred places.
facets.scholarly_note: Drawn only from published, publicly available (non-restricted) material; restricted and secret-sacred knowledge is deliberately excluded. Authority over these narratives rests with the custodians of the relevant Country, and versions differ between language groups.

facets.facet_name: Lightning Man Who Strikes with Stone Axes
facets.core_claim: Namarrkon's axes split the clouds; his storms bring the life-giving wet season and can strike down trees and people.
facets.scholarly_note: Drawn only from published, publicly available (non-restricted) material; restricted and secret-sacred knowledge is deliberately excluded. Authority over these narratives rests with the custodians of the relevant Country, and versions differ between language groups.

facets.facet_name: Serpent Whose Path Made the Rivers
facets.core_claim: The Waagal shaped the waterways of Noongar country and still dwells in them as their guardian.
facets.scholarly_note: Drawn only from published, publicly available (non-restricted) material; restricted and secret-sacred knowledge is deliberately excluded. Authority over these narratives rests with the custodians of the relevant Country, and versions differ between language groups.

facets.facet_name: Serpent Creators of Water and Rain
facets.core_claim: The serpent beings of the creation time made the waterways and live on in them, bringing rain and life and enforcing the law.
facets.scholarly_note: The single label "Rainbow Serpent" is an anthropological grouping; the beings it covers are distinct and Country-specific. Authority over these narratives rests with the custodians of the relevant Country, and versions differ between language groups.

facets.facet_name: Sleeping Ancestor from Whose Body Life Came
facets.core_claim: Karora dreamed in the earth and life came forth from his body; he rests still in the soak at Ilbalintja.
facets.scholarly_note: Drawn only from published, publicly available (non-restricted) material; restricted and secret-sacred knowledge is deliberately excluded. Authority over these narratives rests with the custodians of the relevant Country, and versions differ between language groups.

facets.facet_name: Father Who Decreed That All Must Die
facets.core_claim: Purukupali's grief made death final for all people and founded the pukumani ceremonies with their carved poles.
facets.scholarly_note: Drawn only from published, publicly available (non-restricted) material; restricted and secret-sacred knowledge is deliberately excluded. Authority over these narratives rests with the custodians of the relevant Country, and versions differ between language groups.

facets.facet_name: Bringer of Malo's Law
facets.core_claim: Malo-Bomai gave the Meriam their law: Malo keeps his hands to himself and does not take what belongs to another.
facets.scholarly_note: Only published, non-restricted material is used; the inner Malo-Bomai ceremonies are restricted.

facets.facet_name: King of Ghosts and Queller of Demons
facets.core_claim: Zhong Kui, the scholar denied the first rank for his ugliness who took his own life, was made king of ghosts by the emperor of heaven; his fierce painted image on the door drives demons away.

facets.facet_name: Kitchen God Who Reports to Heaven
facets.core_claim: From the stove Zao Jun watches the household all year; on the 23rd or 24th of the twelfth month he ascends to report its deeds to the Jade Emperor, and his lips are sweetened with malt candy.

facets.facet_name: Duke of Thunder Who Punishes Hidden Crimes
facets.core_claim: With drum, mallet and chisel the bird-faced Lei Gong strikes down those guilty of secret crimes, especially the unfilial and those who waste grain.

facets.facet_name: Mother of Lightning with Her Mirrors
facets.core_claim: Dian Mu flashes her two mirrors to light up the guilty so that Lei Gong's thunderbolt strikes true.

facets.facet_name: Lord of the Soil and Locality
facets.core_claim: Every street, field and village has its Tudigong, the lowest official of the celestial bureaucracy, who guards the place, blesses its harvest and reports to the City God.

facets.facet_name: Thunder Kami Beating the Drums
facets.core_claim: Raijin beats his ring of drums to make thunder and brings the storms and rain on which the rice depends.

facets.facet_name: Wind Kami with the Bag of Winds
facets.core_claim: Fūjin carries the winds in a great bag over his shoulders and releases them across the world.

facets.facet_name: Dragon King of the Sea Palace
facets.core_claim: Ryūjin rules the palace Ryūgū-jō beneath the sea and controls the tides with his jewels of ebb and flow.

facets.facet_name: Mireuk the Creator Cheated of His World (Changse-ga)
facets.core_claim: In the shaman song of creation Mireuk separated heaven and earth and made the first people, but Seokga stole the world from him by cheating in a flower-growing contest; that is why the world is full of thieves and evil.
facets.scholarly_note: From the Changse-ga creation muga recorded in Hamhung in 1923.

facets.facet_name: Mireuk, the Coming Buddha (Korean Maitreya)
facets.core_claim: Mireuk, the future Buddha, will come to establish a world of peace; Koreans carved great Mireuk statues in stone and awaited him in messianic movements.

facets.facet_name: Atua of Cultivated Food and Peace
facets.core_claim: Rongo, son of Rangi and Papa, governs the kūmara and all cultivated food and the peace in which gardens can grow.

facets.facet_name: Hina Who Went to the Moon
facets.core_claim: Weary of endless labor, Hina left the earth for the moon, where she can still be seen beating tapa cloth.

facets.facet_name: Tagaloa-a-Lagi, Creator Above the Heavens
facets.core_claim: Tagaloa-a-Lagi existed alone in the void above the heavens; he made the rocks, the earth and the sea, and sent his daughter, the plover Tuli, to find dry land, from which the islands and people came.

facets.facet_name: Tagaro, Creator and Wise Brother
facets.core_claim: In northern Vanuatu Tagaro made the land, people and good things, while his foolish brother Suqe spoiled them and brought death and hardship.
facets.scholarly_note: Recorded for Maewo and neighboring islands in R. H. Codrington, The Melanesians (1891); the Tagaro–Tangaroa connection is debated.

facets.facet_name: Lord of Wealth and Guardian of the North
facets.core_claim: Kubera, king of the yakshas, keeps the treasures of the earth in his city Alakā and guards the northern quarter.
